Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the EnerGrid Utilities Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to EnerGrid Utilities' Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Strategy Officer; Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Regulatory Officer; and Karen Lee, Chief Communications Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Grid modernization and smart grid initiatives.
    2. Rate base growth and factors impacting growth.
    3. Discussion of regulatory lag and mitigation strategies.
    4. Investments in renewable energy and clean energy transition.
    5. Progress towards clean energy goals and emission reductions.
    6. Overview of financial performance relative to guidance.
    7. Generation fleet performance and availability.
    8. Revenue breakdown by regulated and unregulated segments.

Let me provide some more detail on these eight key aspects. Starting with grid modernization and smart grid initiatives, which form a cornerstone of our five-year capital plan. In the utilities sector, the grid is our backbone, especially with accelerating electrification, renewables integration, and distributed energy resources or DERs. Over the past 12 months, we've deployed about $450 million in capex here, or 15% of total infrastructure spend, including advanced metering infrastructure or AMI, distribution automation, synchrophasor technology, and next-gen SCADA systems. Year-to-date, smart grid-related assets under management rose 22% year-over-year, totaling over 18,000 circuit miles in our Northeast and Mid-Atlantic areas, putting us ahead of peers like Dominion Energy and Exelon.

Our AMI rollout has installed over 2.8 million smart meters, reaching 85% coverage of our 3.3 million customers, up from 62% end of 2022. These are advanced Itron Gen5 Riva platforms with edge computing for real-time communication, demand response, and load forecasting. Reliability has improved sharply: SAIDI fell 18% to 85 minutes, SAIFI by 15% to 0.92 per customer, thanks to 1,200 automated reclosers and 450 capacitor banks using SEL-751 relays.

We've deployed over 350 phasor measurement units or PMUs grid-wide, synced to NERC standards via GE GridOS, cutting cascading outage risks 25% in renewables-heavy areas. This integrates 2.2 GW of DERs like solar and storage, up 35%, aligning with FERC Order 2222 through our virtual power plant pilot with Stem Inc. In the Northeast under PJM, $180 million went to microgrid feeders and hardened substations, reducing restoration times 40% post-Hurricane Ida in places like Philadelphia and Baltimore. In Mid-Atlantic Virginia, $120 million for EV upgrades under the Virginia Clean Economy Act includes 15,000 Level 2 chargers with V2G via ChargePoint, eyeing 20% EV load growth by 2026. Our DOE-funded smart inverter pilots raised hosting capacity 28%, easing duck curve issues.

Financially, we've saved $95 million in OpEx via AI asset management from ABB Ability and AspenTech OSI Monarch, predicting 85% of failures and extending transformer life 15%. O&M per mile dropped 12% to $1,200, with $45 million new revenue from frequency regulation. ROIC is 9.2% versus our 7.5% hurdle, payback 5.2 years. With IRA grants of $75 million plus state incentives, we're budgeting $600 million for 2024 capex, including $200 million cybersecurity via NIST zero-trust from Dragos and Nozomi, amid 30% ransomware spike per E-ISAC. DERMS scales to 5 GW by 2027 with Siemens Spectrum Power. This adds 200 basis points EPS accretion, making us top-quartile in S&P utilities.

Moving to rate base growth and factors impacting it. Our rate base ended Q3 at $26.4 billion, up 8.2% year-over-year from $24.4 billion, on pace for 7-9% full-year to $28.2 billion. Trailing 12-month growth is 7.8%, beating PJM and MISO peers at 6%. Our $2.7 billion 2024 CapEx, up 12%, drives 85% of expansion, with $1.8 billion in service YTD plus $120 million AFUDC at 7.2% WACC.

Transmission ($850 million YTD) tackles NERC and FERC Order 1000, like $450 million Green Valley 345kV upgrade adding 1,200 MW renewables support, part of $3.2 billion five-year plan clearing 95% PJM RPM at $110/MW-day. Distribution ($650 million) covers hardening, AMI, DER hosting with smart inverters on 45% circuits for 12% peak solar. Clean transition ($300 million) includes 350 MW solar like Ridgeview (150 MW First Solar bifacial, $28/MWh PPA) and 150 MW/300 MWh Indiana BESS with Tesla Megapack for arbitrage and regulation.

Regulatory formula rates and forward-test-year cases yield 6.5% escalators, like $250 million Indiana rider at 10.35% ROE. Transmission formula adds $45 million CWIP. Midwest tailwinds: Ohio data centers add 2.5% customers, MISO favors coal-to-gas. Load grew 4.1% retail, C&I 6.2% from AWS, EVs (15 GW managed charging), heat pumps, Intel fab pushing peaks 15% by 2028, needing $1.5 billion upgrades.

Offsetting: depreciation up 11% to $650 million annualized, coal retirements like 400 MW Harding cut 0.5%, but repowering offsets. Inflation 8-10% mitigated by fixed EPC (85%) and domestic GE Vernova. Five-year $14-16 billion CapEx eyes 8%+ CAGR via resilience (ACCC conductors), decarbonization (1.2 GW renewables), load monetization. PJM queue risks via fast-track.

Next, regulatory lag and mitigation strategies. This delay between costs and rate recovery pressures ROE 100-200 bps, contributing $175 million headwind past 24 months in Illinois/Indiana from 9-12 month lags and supply disruptions inflating costs 15-20%. TTM ROE 9.4% vs 10.25% authorized, lag 50 bps, like Ameren/NiSource.

PJM formula rates minimize to 6 months for $450 million HVDC. MISO North 11 months, Indiana 8. Mitigations: three rate cases since 2022 securing $1.2 billion at 7-month lag; pending Indiana $650 million with 40% CWIP solar. Riders: FPPC 102% recovery shielding $120 million gas volatility; REAMs pass 90% PTC/ITC; Illinois tracker $280 million smart grid.

PBR pilots in Indiana tie to SAIDI/SAIFI for 50 bps ROE upside, like Eversource. BESS Order 841, nuclear uprates $200 million IRA credits, CCUS 45Q trackers. Advocating MYRPs, Illinois formula rates add 75 bps. Merchant 15% hedges $90 million. Lag to 25 bps 2025, supporting 6-8% EPS with $3.2 billion capex.

On investments in renewable energy and clean energy transition, we've committed $12.5 billion since 2020, $4.2 billion YTD or 45% of $9.3 billion capex. Renewables at 18.2 GW operating, up 25%, 42% of 43 GW fleet vs EIA 28%. Solar 9.8 GW, wind 6.1 GW, BESS 1.7 GW/4.3 GWh, other 0.6 GW. Added 2.4 GW H1: 650 MW SunForge Texas ERCOT, 400 MW Prairie Winds SPP.

Unlevered IRR 9.2%, solar 10.1% at $28/MWh LCOE down 15% YoY. Wind $32/MWh, 42% CF. 92% new capacity 12-20 year PPAs with IG off-takers like AWS/Microsoft, 85% 2025-2027 output $42/MWh hedged. Co-location 70% solar+BESS like 300 MW/1.2 GWh Desert Peak CAISO adds 18% yield, ancillaries $15/kW-year. Grid-forming inverters FERC 2222. Offshore $450 million, 200 MW Carolinas with Ørsted to 2 GW $60/MWh.

Diversified: Southeast 4 GW solar IRA ITC; ERCOT 3.2 GW data/Bitcoin/EV; Midwest PTC wind; West geothermal Ormat. Europe 15% capex, 1.2 GW UK JV RWE. IRA $2.1 billion credits. 60/30/10 mix 2030: SMRs NuScale 300 MW $65/MWh, H2 Plug Power. Mitigate queues, polysilicon via ahead orders, Fluence software. ROE 11.5%, $0.45 EPS 2025.

Progress towards clean energy goals and emission reductions: 17% YoY Scope 1/2 GHG drop to 28 million MT CO2e YTD, on 50% from 2005 by 2030, net-zero 2045 ahead peers. Scope 3 down 12% GHG Protocol. Renewables 42% mix, 45 TWh YTD, added 1.2 GW Q3: 800 MW ERCOT solar, 400 MW PJM wind, 12 GW pipeline.

BESS 450 MW/1,800 MWh CAISO/ERCOT 92% RTE, firms 25% VRE, cuts fossil 8%. 100 MW H2 pilot Illinois 200 tons/year, 20-30% turbine blend NOx -40%. CCS 50 MW Heritage MHI amine 100k tons 95% capture, 45Q $85/ton + RECs.

ERCOT 55% clean dispatch emissions -22%, 10-yr PPAs Google/Meta $45/MWh. CAISO retire 300 MW gas, BESS DR SO2 -35% $50M LCFS. PJM/MISO offshore 800 MW Garden State 48% CF Mid-Atlantic -10%. IRA $370B lowers LCOE 15-20%, 85% hedged 28-30% EBITDA. Queues mitigate $2.5B upgrades, 150 MW community solar. $15B decade engine, 60% EPS growth.

Our overview of financial performance relative to guidance: Q3 adjusted EBITDA $825 million, +12% YoY beating $750-800M midpoint 8%, YTD $1.55B toward high-end $3.1-3.3B. GAAP NI $450M $1.12/share vs $0.95-1.05 guided; adjusted EPS $1.18 +15% YoY. Revenue $2.65B +9% vs $2.5B mid.

Regulated (65% EBITDA) $580M +5% vs guided, sales 18.5M MWh +4.2%, C&I +6% data centers 1.2 GW PPAs, 10.1% ROE Virginia case, $450M rate base. Renewables (25%) $185M +14% vs guided, 4.5 GW 32% CF, 300 MW Blue Ridge 85%, 450 MW BESS $15M PJM. Thermal (10%) $60M inline, spreads $28/MWh hedged $2.80 natgas, coal retire Salem Harbor -1.2M tons CO2 $12M save.

Beats from volumes/pricing +5.1% load C&I +7% EV/AI; O&M +3% vs 5% guided predictive/drone; synchrophasor/ADMS 99.97% reliability +250 MW PJM. ISO-NE FCA $10.50/kW-mo. Raising FY24: EBITDA $3.25-3.45B, EPS $4.85-5.05.

Generation fleet performance and availability: Fleet EAF 92.3% +150 bps YoY, forced outages -25% 1,200 hours, CF 68.4%, gen 42.7 TWh +6%. Thermal gas 15 GW 94.1% EAF GE/Siemens H-class heat rate 6,650 Btu/kWh, peakers 96.2% ERCOT ramps. Coal 88.5% planned. Nuclear 4 BWRs 95.7% CF 96.1% 8.2 TWh. Renewables 98.5% EAF wind 42.3% solar 24.8% +250 MW BESS +12% output 4.1 TWh +18%.

PJM 93.8% $45M ancillaries; ERCOT strong heat dome no curtail; MISO 90.2% cyber drill. FleetFit $250M: Predix/MindSphere -30% outages, 15% H2 blend, drone blades, Emerson/Honeywell MTTR 48 hrs, EFOR 2.1% vs 3.5%. Retire last coal 2025, 2 GW clean capex 75/25 mix 2030 IRA $150M. FY24 EAF 92-93%.

Finally, revenue breakdown by regulated and unregulated segments. FY24 on track $16B+, Q3 regulated 71% $10.8B annualized +6.1%, T&D PJM/MISO/SPP ROE 9.8%. Base/riders $450M new rates Virginia/Ohio 10.25%/9.75%, dist $7.2B +5.4% +120k cust EV/heat pumps; trans $3.1B +12% FERC formula $1.2B AFUDC $2.8B capex Apex-PJM 500kV +2GW Order 679. Northeast +9%, Midwest +7%, SPP weather.

Unregulated 29% $4.4B +14.7%, power/marketing $2.9B +16% spreads $28/MWh PJM/ERCOT nuclear 93.5% Q4 BRA $270/MW-day $250M arbitrage $180M; renewables/storage $1.3B +22% 2.5 GW solar Texas Google PPA IRA $350M BESS $250M +40% CAISO RA 12% IRR H2 pilot; other $200M. Margins reg 28.5% +150bps AMI SAIDI -15%; unreg 32% hedged 70/30. 5-7% reg CAGR $12B capex, 10-12% unreg 80% hedged/PPA.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss the financials.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported earnings per share of $1.25 and revenue of $2.8 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $750 million, primarily focused on grid modernization and renewable expansions. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate mid-single digit EPS growth in 2025.

Mike Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbines power plants due to the implementation of predictive maintenance AI. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 20%.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Mike. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery energy storage systems space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the Midwest market.

Dr. Raj Singh: Thank you, Elena. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed Dragos platform to enhance our defenses against cyber threats. We are also piloting advanced distribution management systems in Ohio.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Dr. Singh. On the regulatory front, we received approval for our rate case settlement in PJM Interconnection. This will allow us to recover $250 million in new rates.

Karen Lee: Thank you, Tom. We are pleased to announce that our community outreach program in Philadelphia has resulted in a 30% increase in positive sentiment towards EnerGrid Utilities.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Lisa, Mike, Elena, Dr. Raj, Tom, and Karen. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for renewable energy expansion?

John Ramirez: Certainly. As detailed earlier, we're aggressively growing our renewables to 18.2 GW with strong IRRs, PPAs, and hybrids, adding GW-scale projects backed by IRA incentives and targeting 60% clean mix by 2030.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee: What is your outlook for rate base growth?

Lisa Chen: We're on track for 7-9% growth this year driven by $2.7 billion CapEx in transmission, distribution, and clean energy, with regulatory mechanisms ensuring timely recovery and 8%+ CAGR ahead.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: How are you mitigating risks related to regulatory lag?

Mike Patel: We've shortened lag through accelerated filings, riders like REAMs and trackers, PBR pilots, and advocacy for multi-year plans, targeting just 25 bps dilution next year.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: What is the anticipated impact of grid modernization on your earnings?

Tom Reilly: These initiatives deliver 9.2% ROIC, $95 million OpEx savings, $45 million new revenues, and 200 bps EPS accretion, with $600 million more capex next year enhancing returns.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to John Ramirez for closing remarks.

John Ramirez: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning EnerGrid Utilities for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in EnerGrid Utilities.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
